item.content:encoded:
EAM Jaishankar meets Russian President Putin as part of his two-day official visit to Moscow External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow as part of his two-day official visit to the country at the invitation of First Deputy Prime Minister of the Russian Federation Denis Manturov. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 17:29 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 17:29 IST

Russian President Vladimir Putin shakes hands with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar during a meeting at the Kremlin in Moscow (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Russia

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin in Moscow as part of his two-day official visit to the country at the invitation of First Deputy Prime Minister of the Russian Federation Denis Manturov. Jaishankar is on an official visit from August 23 to August 24. As per the release from the Ministry of External Affairs, the EAM will co-chair the 27th Session of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC). As per the release issued on Saturday, "The External Affairs Minister, S. Jaishankar, will undertake an official visit to Russia on 23-24 August 2026 to co-chair the 27th Session of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC)." During the visit, Jaishankar will also meet the Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation, Sergey Lavrov and exchange perspectives on regional and global issues. "During the visit, EAM will also meet Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation H.E. Mr. Sergey Lavrov and exchange perspectives on regional and global issues," the release added. India and Russia have a longstanding and time-tested partnership. A prior release by the Ministry of External Affairs noted that since the signing of the "Declaration on the India-Russia Strategic Partnership" in October 2000, India-Russia ties have acquired a qualitatively new character with enhanced levels of cooperation in almost all areas, including political, security, defence, trade and economy, science & technology, culture, and people-to-people ties. Under the Strategic Partnership, several institutionalised dialogue mechanisms operate at both political and official levels to ensure regular interaction and follow-up on cooperation activities. The India-Russia Intergovernmental Commission (IRIGC) has two divisions: the Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC), co-chaired by External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar from India and First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov from Russia; and the Military and Military-Technical Cooperation (IRIGC-M&MTC), headed by the Defence Ministers of the two countries. The bilateral relationship between the two countries has remained strong and stable over the years. MEA underlined how the India-Russia partnership has been among the steadiest in the contemporary era, with a shared commitment to a multipolar world as well as to expanding engagement beyond the traditional military, nuclear and space cooperation. (ANI)

item.title: India eyes 14-fold jump in electronic component production by FY31: Report
item.description: India is looking to sharply increase its electronic component production as the country's total electronics production is targeted to reach USD 500 billion by FY31, according to a report by Kotak ...
item.content:encoded:
India eyes 14-fold jump in electronic component production by FY31: Report India is looking to sharply increase its electronic component production as the country's total electronics production is targeted to reach USD 500 billion by FY31, according to a report by Kotak Mutual Fund. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 15:19 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 15:19 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India is looking to sharply increase its electronic component production as the country's total electronics production is targeted to reach USD 500 billion by FY31, according to a report by Kotak Mutual Fund. The report showed that electronic component production is projected to rise from USD 10.5 billion in FY24 to USD 150 billion by FY31. This represents a more than 14-fold increase over the period. The expected rise in component production stands out as one of the major changes in India's electronics manufacturing landscape. While mobile phone production is also projected to grow significantly, the increase in electronic components is expected to be much faster. According to the report, mobile phone production stood at USD 51 billion in FY24 and is estimated to rise to USD 159 billion by FY31. This means mobile phone production is expected to more than triple during the period. The report's projections indicate that electronic components could become a much larger part of India's overall electronics production by FY31. Component production is expected to increase by around USD 139.5 billion during the period, compared with an increase of USD 108 billion in mobile phone production. The report also estimates that mobile phones will remain the largest category, with production expected to increase from USD 51 billion in FY24 to USD 159 billion by FY31. Consumer electronics, including televisions, audio products and accessories, are projected to rise from USD 13 billion to USD 36 billion during the same period. IT hardware, including laptops and tablets, is expected to increase from USD 5 billion in FY24 to USD 32 billion by FY31. Wearables and hearables are projected to rise from USD 2.5 billion to USD 38 billion, while auto electronics could increase from USD 8 billion to USD 33 billion. Telecom equipment production is estimated to grow from USD 3.5 billion to USD 15 billion. The report also projects the 'Others' category to rise from USD 21.5 billion to USD 37 billion. The projections show that while India's mobile phone manufacturing sector is expected to remain a major part of the electronics industry, the country's growth ambition increasingly includes a wider range of products and electronic components. The sharp projected rise in component production, from USD 10.5 billion to USD 150 billion, therefore stands out in the report's estimates as India targets total electronic production of USD 500 billion by FY31. (ANI)

item.title: Tanker on fire off Saudi Arabia coast after strike by unknown projectile, says UKMTO
item.description: A tanker caught fire following a projectile strike near Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port, with UKMTO confirming all crew are safe. The incident coincides with escalating Houthi strikes on Red Sea shipping ...
item.content:encoded:
Tanker on fire off Saudi Arabia coast after strike by unknown projectile, says UKMTO A tanker caught fire following a projectile strike near Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port, with UKMTO confirming all crew are safe. The incident coincides with escalating Houthi strikes on Red Sea shipping routes and Saudi military targets, including recent missile and drone operations off Mocha and in Marib. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 15:05 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 15:05 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A tanker caught fire after being hit by an unidentified projectile off the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia on Monday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). The incident took place about 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu, one of Saudi Arabia's key oil ports on the Red Sea. The UKMTO, a British maritime security agency, said the vessel's crew were safe and accounted for, with no reports of an environmental impact. The port has assumed heightened strategic importance as vessels look for alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing disruptions in that maritime passage. Security concerns surrounding shipping corridors in the Red Sea have also intensified. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group has threatened Saudi-affiliated vessels and previously claimed attacks against installations run by Saudi oil giant Aramco located in Yanbu, including an alleged strike in July. The latest development follows a series of recent strikes in the region. Earlier on August 17, the Houthi group stated that it had launched a ballistic missile attack targeting a Saudi military landing ship alongside four escort vessels in the Red Sea, off the southwestern port city of Mocha. Detailing that operation, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree noted that the attack was executed using multiple ballistic missiles, describing the strikes as "direct and precise". He asserted that the landing vessel caught fire, while some escorting boats sank and others were set ablaze. In a separate statement, Saree added that Houthi forces targeted a military weapons depot at the Sahn al-Jin camp in Yemen's northeastern Marib province using several drones, claiming the strike caused a fire at the location. Mocha, a government-held port city near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and sits close to a major global maritime chokepoint. Repeated Houthi attacks in and around the city since August 9 have reportedly caused casualties and damage to port infrastructure while disrupting shipping operations. Refusing to back down, the Houthis have said they are closely monitoring Saudi military movements and will continue targeting Saudi forces on land and at sea. The group has described the campaign as part of its policy of "siege for siege" against Saudi Arabia. (ANI)

item.title: Fresh USD 22 million to sustain education for crisis-affected children in Sudan
item.description: Taking cognizance of the humanitarian and displacement crisis, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), an organisation within the United Nations and administered under the rules of the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF ...
item.content:encoded:
Fresh USD 22 million to sustain education for crisis-affected children in Sudan Taking cognizance of the humanitarian and displacement crisis, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), an organisation within the United Nations and administered under the rules of the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF), committed to a fresh USD 22 million multi-year investment to help "restore safe, quality and inclusive education" for affected children, a press release said. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 14:18 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 14:18 IST

Sudanese refugees gather at Adre hospital in Chad as Doctors Without Borders (MSF) teams provide medical assistance to war-wounded patients from West Darfur, Sudan. (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Sudan's civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023 has triggered forcible internal displacement of millions and widespread hunger. The war in Sudan has entered its fourth year now, majorly affecting crucial aspects of civilian lives, including the education of nearly 2,00,000 children and teenagers, in regions across West Darfur, South Kordofan and Gedaref. Thousands of families fled to displacement camps in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state in south-central Sudan, after the RSF attacked villages across southern and western parts of the region, Al Jazeera reported on August 21. Taking cognizance of the humanitarian and displacement crisis, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), an organisation within the United Nations and administered under the rules of the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF), committed to a fresh USD 22 million multi-year investment to help "restore safe, quality and inclusive education" for affected children, a press release said. This announcement comes after ECW director Maysa Jalbout met the crisis-affected civilians, including children and teachers. They have been affected by more than three years of armed conflict and displacement. Since 2023, at least 14 million people have been internally displaced in Sudan, while nearly 33.7 million people require humanitarian assistance as a result of the ongoing war between the SAF and the RSF. The RSF emerged in 2013 from the Janjaweed, a militia group that was supported by the Sudanese government during the War in Darfur, which began in 2003. The civil war has forced at least 8 million children, which amounts to nearly half of Sudan's 17 million school-age children, out of school since the schools across the country remain non-operational given the sustained conflict. According to ECW, some crisis-affected children in Sudan have missed nearly 500 days of schooling due to the ongoing conflict. The ECW investment will not only support the restoration of education and learning environments, but also help children regain a sense of "safety and normalcy" amid the disruption and trauma caused by the war. "Education in Sudan has been interrupted by conflict, displacement and unimaginable hardship. Yet it remains one of the most powerful tools we have to protect millions of children, restore hope and support recovery," the ECW director said in a press release. "This investment is about much more than reopening classrooms. It is about supporting children to regain a sense of safety and normalcy while strengthening education systems that can continue serving communities through crisis and into recovery. Sudan's children cannot wait," she added. ECW's program aims to support those most affected by Sudan's civil war, including displaced children, refugees, and vulnerable host communities. At least 60% of the beneficiaries will be girls and 10% will be children with disabilities. The program will provide mental health and psychosocial support while establishing safe formal and non-formal learning environments. An additional $5 million will be kept flexible so that the program can respond quickly if new conflicts, disasters, or climate-related emergencies occur, ECW said, adding that the implementation of the same will be led by Save the Children, an internationally renowned NGO, in collaboration with local partners and others. Save the Children Deputy Country Director Francesco Lanino said that ECW's multi-year investment will provide children in Sudan access to learning and critical support for "recovery." "For millions of children in Sudan, conflict and displacement have disrupted not only their education, but also their sense of safety, routine and hope for the future. Access to safe, quality education is a fundamental right and one of the most effective ways to protect children and support their recovery during times of crisis," Save the Children Deputy Country Director Francesco Lanino said in a press release. "Through this ECW multi-year investment and partnership, children in Sudan will be able to access learning opportunities that provide critical protection, psychosocial support and a pathway to recovery, resilience and a brighter future," he added. The 48 per cent of the budget will be given to national and local partners in Sudan, ECW said, adding that local actors will work alongside concerned organisations, including Alsalam Organisation for Relief and Development (AORD), to "ensure the response is rooted in the priorities and capacities of the communities it serves". "Communities in Sudan have shown extraordinary resilience despite the immense challenges they continue to face. As a Sudanese organisation, we know that lasting impact comes from solutions that are rooted in local knowledge, trust and partnerships with the communities we serve," AORD general director Rudwan Elfaki said in a press statement. "Through this program, we will work alongside families, teachers and local partners to help children return to safe, inclusive learning environments where they can recover, regain hope and build the skills they need for the future," he added. ECW's USD 22 million investment provides seed funding towards a total program requirement of USD 39 million. (ANI)
